■Stage Direction
Age: High school 2nd year
Personality: Hard worker

...I don't mind slow-roasting something, but if it goes cold, it defeats the whole point.
—Watch this.
—Don't make me laugh.

...She's my junior.
Quit putting stupid nonsense into her head.

From what I have observed of your current training,
the workload appears to be somewhat excessive.

That's the end of your little rebellion.
The pecking order is clear—

The training plans she drew up were always flawless.
Without a better proposal to offer, I hesitated to even speak up.

—Right, a wager. Whoever loses does whatever the winner says.
Simple enough rules, yeah?

...Fine then. If you've sprouted an ego...
this is the perfect chance to put you in your place.
Talk, huh.

You said you wanted to talk to me, right?
Then... you'll have to earn your seat at the table.

...Phew. That's it for today.
Good work. You can head home too.
...Hmph.

Both belonging to the Symboli family and with parents tied to the URA,
I had heard they crossed paths frequently ever since they were children.

I know that... but still—I've made up my mind!
Now that my true potential is blooming, I want to do everything I can...!!

From now on, you obey me.
...You got that drilled into your head, right?

—In that instant.
Just when I thought she radiated the same explosive aura as during her races—

If you continue at this rate, you may not remain unscathed.
Surely your legs know that better than anyone, do they not?
Hm? Hey, you... You're Sirius-senpai's—

Sirius Symboli's training is progressing smoothly, with no room for me to interject.
Perhaps I shouldn't be meddling unnecessarily after all—

With this, the dynamic between us has been set in stone.
If only I hadn't let myself get swept into a match from the start and properly asserted my desire to talk things out...

I watch Sirius Symboli walk away in silence.
In the end, from the day we signed the contract until now, we haven't had a single real conversation...

Normally, hitting out of order is a foul, but... as a handicap, I'll allow you up to three fouls.
You can pocket them in any order you like. Cake walk, right?

Well, well... what an unexpected guest.
What do you want? Don't tell me you're looking to play with fire?

Come on, I'll let you go first.
...Naturally, you're not backing down, are you?

Still, this is my chance. If I win, I can create an opening for us to talk.
I have a handicap too, so there has to be a way.

...Hm. While that willpower deserves respect,
as the Student Council President, I must—

For a while after that,
training proceeded strictly according to Sirius Symboli's own methods.
...Another miss, huh.

!
That's...

Heh, don't make such a gloomy face.
Come on, pack your things. Gotta take you out for a walk once in a while...

However—things don't go smoothly at all. With each failure, my palms grow sweatier,
making the cue shake even more.

The balls scatter in all directions, sinking into the pockets one after another,
until finally, the 9-ball drops—!
Hah—...ngh!!
(—Clack, roll roll...)

You really think a collared pet
can sink its fangs into its owner so easily?

—Nine-ball... A game where you strike balls in numerical order from 1 to 9,
and whoever pockets the 9-ball wins.
—What is it?
...Hey.

Hearing voices nearby, I turn around to see Symboli Rudolf talking to a student.
Come to think of it, she is—

I broke the chain. Biting back or tucking your tail and running—
the rest is up to you to "choose."

Hm? Who're you?
That badge... Don't tell me you're a Trainer?

Whether out of sheer whim, or simply to amuse herself with my dejection...
I walked back to the academy together with Sirius Symboli. And then—

—The moment her words from that day crossed my mind,
before I could even organize my thoughts... my legs had already started moving.

I ended up letting Sirius Symboli sweep me into accepting the match...
I didn't want to make her obey me... I just wanted to talk things out.
—Allow me to offer an objective perspective.
